image_description: A young female musician in a red marching band uniform holding a large, dark wooden wind instrument (bassoon) vertically. She is smiling and looking slightly to her left. In the background, other band members in similar uniforms are visible, along with flags and music stands. The setting appears to be an outdoor performance or parade.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument extends from the bottom of the frame well above the subject's head, indicating significant length consistent with a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the bell points upward, the 'U-shape' (the butt joint at the bottom where the tube doubles back) is not clearly visible due to the angle and occlusion by the subject's body/hands. The instrument appears as a straight vertical column from this perspective.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is invisible. The external doubling back (butt joint) is occluded or not clearly resolved in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the instrument is cut off by the upper edge of the image frame; the bocal is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver metal keywork is clearly visible on the lower joint held by the subject's right hand and partially on the wing joint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell flare is not fully visible (cut off). The instrument is held vertically/diagonally, but the 'diagonal across body' posture is partially obscured by the framing and the subject's stance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument body exhibits a dark, polished wood grain consistent with maple or rosewood used in bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible keys are silver-colored metal.
The main body segments are clearly constructed from turned wood.

artifact_observations.location: Left hand/finger area on the instrument
artifact_observations.reasoning: The subject's left hand (holding the upper part of the instrument) appears somewhat indistinct. The fingers seem to merge slightly with the black wood of the instrument, lacking clear separation boundaries typical of high-resolution photography. It looks like a mild AI generation blur or fusion.

The faces in the background (especially the boy in the center-right) have a slightly 'waxy' or over-smoothed texture compared to the foreground subject, suggesting potential generative artifacts in depth-of-field rendering.

To rigorously check the boundary between the fingers and the instrument for fusion or melting artifacts, which were suspected in the Router phase.
To verify if the background elements have consistent geometric depth and do not exhibit warping or spatial inconsistencies common in AI-generated crowds.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts missed by specific auditors.

focus_areas: Verification of finger-instrument boundary integrity (no fusion)
Consistency of wood grain texture on the instrument
